text: {"headline":"Provider 1000000480 bills 99215 well above expectation in every complexity tier, including patients with no chronic conditions, but the 19 returned 99215 charts all support the billed level.","leaning":"inconclusive","interpretation":"The excess is not explained by a sicker panel: the 99215 share runs roughly three times the all-provider rate in every tier, from 0 conditions to 5+, and sampled low-complexity 99215s such as C0245131 (Z09 follow-up), C0245477 (J06.9 upper respiratory infection) and C0245645 (R21 rash) carry diagnoses that rarely need high-complexity decision-making. Against that, none of the documented 99215 claims fell below the billed level (examples C0245638 and C0245985 show high MDM and over 40 minutes). By the standard rule, that pattern points away from upcoding, so the two lines of evidence conflict. The documentation is a thin 3% sample, and it may reflect cloned or inflated notes rather than real complexity: problem-list signals appear on 20% of notes (including C0245556, a 0-condition R10.9 abdominal pain 99215), and time entries repeat on 12.5%. No audit trail was received, so cloning cannot be ruled out. A reviewer should first request the charts and audit trails specifically for the low-complexity 99215 claims listed here, and check whether their MDM and time documentation is templated or copied across visits."}
